title: Sub-2nm high-NA EUV scanner throughput and uptime
bottleneck: High-NA EUV scanners (ASML EXE, 0.55 NA) can print sub-2nm features in a single exposure, but their throughput, uptime, and cost are unsolved at production scale. Each tool costs over $350 million, draws roughly 1,400 kW, and needs months of calibration by hundreds of engineers before stable high-volume manufacturing. Reduced depth of focus forces thinner resists and near-perfect overlay, shrinking the process window so much that line yield at 2nm-class nodes remains fragile.
why_it_blocks: Sub-2nm logic is the backbone of next-generation AI accelerators and edge AI; if high-NA EUV cannot deliver reliable wafers-per-hour at acceptable defect rates, the entire industry roadmap stalls with no Plan B, since extreme multi-patterning with older tools is economically infeasible.
current_state: First high-NA systems were delivered to Intel, TSMC, and Samsung in 2024-2025 for process development, with high-volume manufacturing targeted for 2026-2027. ASML has confirmed Hyper-NA (0.75 NA) feasibility for 2030s nodes, but the ecosystem of resists, pellicles, and metrology is still maturing.
